limitations.DR-009: Behavior outside the Context precondition is not assigned a conformance outcome.
limitations.DR-011: Finite tests do not establish or refute all real-time bounds; none is promised.
limitations.DR-012: 32 queued requests test finite backlog behavior, not mathematical unboundedness.

clauses.caller_cleanup: Cancel an abandoned pending request and consume its result. Do not call Release for a failed Acquire; any own reservation is rolled back before error return.
clauses.no_auto_reclaim: Every successful acquisition requires matching release after protected work ends, even if its Context is canceled later. Cancellation does not automatically reclaim a successful holding.
clauses.instance_lifetime: Creating a new semaphore does not cancel pending work or release holdings on an old instance.
clauses.independent_calls: Each invocation is a separate acquisition, including repeat calls from the same logical caller. No deduplication, replacement or reentrant success is provided.
clauses.self_blocking: A caller holding capacity can block itself by awaiting another acquisition before releasing its existing holding.
clauses.shared_context: Independent requests can share a Context, in which case cancellation can affect all of them.
clauses.transferable_release: Release responsibility may transfer to another goroutine. The application must match releases to actually held, not already released capacity.
clauses.aggregate_only: The semaphore checks aggregate holdings, not caller identity. A duplicate release may remain undetected while other holdings cover it; this is a detection limit, not permission to release twice.
clauses.receiver_selection: The caller selects the receiver. Release affects only that instance; release responsibility can transfer but capacity cannot transfer across instances.
clauses.context_selection: The supplied Context governs the request. The semaphore does not infer a different intended Context.
clauses.context_precondition: Acquire requires a non-nil Context conforming to the Go Context contract. Conforming custom implementations are supported, including concurrent-safe methods, stable Done and consistent cancellation errors.
clauses.nil_done_valid: A nil Done channel is valid for a Context that cannot be canceled; it is distinct from a nil Context.
clauses.no_fault_recovery_contract: No automatic substitution, repair, panic recovery or additional progress guarantee is promised for faulty, blocking or reentrant custom Context methods.
clauses.initial_cancel: For a valid nonnegative weight, closed Done at the initial under-lock check causes a Context error without acquisition. Negative weights retain DR-002 panic priority; oversized errors retain DR-004 rules.
clauses.queued_cancel: Processing queued cancellation removes the request or reverses a grant that raced with cleanup before returning the Context error.
clauses.grant_rollback: A queued request receiving a grant checks cancellation again; if cancellation is observed, its grant is returned before error return.
clauses.late_cancel_success: Cancellation after the last applicable checkpoint may coexist with nil return. That success retains its release obligation. Grant notification alone is not successful API return.
clauses.transient_reservation: An error return leaves no own holding or queue entry. Temporary reservations may affect other operations; global state and observations need not be unchanged.
clauses.try_no_queue: TryAcquire obtains the synchronized state, checks once whether admission is permitted, and returns false if not. It does not join the capacity queue or await a future release.
clauses.mutex_wait_allowed: Internal mutex waiting is permitted. Context cancellation does not interrupt mutex acquisition; cancellation is processed at the defined checkpoints.
clauses.no_latency_bound: No fixed return or cancellation-latency bound is promised. A Context deadline does not guarantee that Acquire has already returned at that instant.
clauses.fifo_enqueue: Queued grants follow enqueue order, not wall-clock method-entry order.
clauses.no_bypass: A blocked head cannot be bypassed by later smaller requests or new Acquire/TryAcquire calls, including zero-weight requests. FIFO can leave capacity idle and does not promise progress without required releases.
clauses.return_order: Grant order does not guarantee goroutine execution order or API-return order.
clauses.no_queue_cap: There is no internal waiter-count cap. The application controls incoming work and cancels obsolete requests; the semaphore bounds held capacity, not queue length.
clauses.zero_release_noop: Release(0) is permitted and is a logical no-op for capacity, queue and grants in valid reachable states. Internal mutex waiting remains permitted.
clauses.no_wakeup_api: Release(0) is not a promised wakeup, repair, flush or extra synchronization API. Progress must follow the actual enabling event, including DR-001 head removal.
